name: WebApplicationCompromise
description: A case template for handling suspected or confirmed web application compromise incidents, including validation, scoping, evidence preservation, attack-path analysis, containment, remediation, provider coordination, impact assessment, and post-incident follow-up.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership. Describe the nature of the compromise (e.g. SQL injection, remote code execution, authentication bypass, web shell), the affected application and environment, how and when it was identified, whether data or credentials were accessed, and current response status. Typically two to four paragraphs.]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation — which applications, hosts, environments, and time periods were examined, what was explicitly excluded, and any limitations on log availability, application telemetry, or environment access that constrained findings.]**

## Technical Analysis — MITRE ATT&CK® Framework

**[Map investigative findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Complete each subsection with specific techniques, evidence, and timeline data. Remove tactics where no activity was observed and note the absence explicitly.]**

### TA0001 — Initial Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application, T1078 Valid Accounts, T1195 Supply Chain Compromise]**

**Vulnerability class:** <!-- SQLi / RCE / Auth bypass / File upload / SSRF / Deserialization / Command injection / API abuse / Credential compromise / Other -->

**CVE / Advisory:** <!-- if applicable -->

**[Describe how the application was compromised — the vulnerability exploited, the affected endpoint or component, and the timestamp of first confirmed malicious activity. Reference key exploit requests from web server or WAF logs where available.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Source IP | Method | URI / Endpoint | Payload Summary | Response Code | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|--------|---------------|----------------|--------------|----------------|
| | | GET / POST / PUT / Other | | | | |

### TA0003 — Persistence

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1505.003 Web Shell, T1053.003 Cron, T1136 Create Account, T1543 Create or Modify System Process]**

**[Describe persistence mechanisms identified — web shells, backdoor scripts, malicious plugins, rogue admin accounts, cron jobs, or modified application templates. Include file paths, hashes, and creation timestamps where available.]**

| Host | Mechanism | Path / Detail | SHA-256 | Date Created | Status |
|------|-----------|--------------|---------|--------------|--------|
| | Web shell / Backdoor / Cron job / Plugin / Account / Modified file / Other | | | | Confirmed / Removed / Pending |

### TA0004 — Privilege Escalation

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation, T1078 Valid Accounts, T1548 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism]**

**[Detail any privilege escalation from the web application context to higher-privilege OS, database, or cloud roles. Note if the web application process ran with excessive privileges that enabled direct escalation.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Host | From | To | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|------|------|----|----------------|
| | | | Web app context / Low-priv user | OS shell / DB admin / Root / Cloud role | |

### TA0005 — Defense Evasion

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1070 Indicator Removal, T1036 Masquerading, T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information, T1562 Impair Defenses]**

**[Describe techniques used to avoid detection — obfuscated web shells, log tampering, masquerading files as legitimate application components, disabling security tooling, or WAF evasion techniques.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Host | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0006 — Credential Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1552 Unsecured Credentials, T1003 OS Credential Dumping, T1555 Credentials from Password Stores, T1528 Steal Application Access Token]**

**[Document any credentials, secrets, API keys, tokens, or database passwords accessed or exposed — including hardcoded credentials in source code, credentials in config files, environment variables, or application logs.]**

| Secret / Credential | Type | Location Found | Exposed To | Rotated? |
|--------------------|------|---------------|------------|----------|
| | API key / DB password / Token / SSH key / OAuth secret / Other | Config file / Env var / Source code / Log / Memory | | Yes / No / Pending |

### TA0008 — Lateral Movement

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1021 Remote Services, T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services, T1550 Use Alternate Authentication Material]**

**[Describe any movement from the compromised application to other systems — using harvested credentials to access databases, internal services, cloud management APIs, or other environments. Omit if lateral movement was not observed.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Source | Destination | Account / Credential Used | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|--------|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|
| | | Web server / App container | Database / Internal service / Cloud / Other environment | | |

### TA0010 — Exfiltration

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1048 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol, T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel, T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service]**

**Exfiltration confirmed:** <!-- Yes / No / Under investigation -->

**Estimated volume:** <!-- e.g. ~200,000 records / ~3 GB / Unknown -->

**[Describe any confirmed or suspected data exfiltration — database dumps, file downloads, outbound transfers, or data returned directly in HTTP responses. Identify data types at risk and regulatory sensitivity where relevant.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Source Host | Destination IP / Domain | Protocol / Method | Volume | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|------------|------------------------|------------------|--------|-----------------|
| | | | HTTP response / DNS / FTP / Cloud upload / Other | | |

**Data types at risk:**

| Data Type | Location | Estimated Volume | Regulatory Classification |
|-----------|----------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| | | | |

---

## Affected Application and Environment

**[Summarise the affected application, components, environments, and downstream systems. Reference the Application and Environment Scope notes for full detail.]**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Application / URL** | |
| **Vulnerability / CVE** | |
| **Affected component** | |
| **Environment** | <!-- Production / Staging / Dev --> |
| **Application status** | <!-- Online / Offline / Degraded / Restricted --> |
| **Downstream systems impacted** | <!-- Yes / No / Under investigation --> |
| **CI/CD pipeline involvement** | <!-- Yes / No / Under investigation --> |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Patch or disable the exploited vulnerability and confirm the access path is closed | | Critical | |
| 2 | Remove all identified web shells, backdoors, malicious plugins, and modified files | | Critical | |
| 3 | Rotate all exposed credentials, API keys, secrets, and database passwords | | Critical | |
| 4 | Revoke sessions and disable any unauthorized accounts created during the compromise | | Critical | |
| 5 | Validate application integrity against a known-good baseline or redeploy from clean source | | Critical | |
| 6 | Assess downstream system impact and rotate any credentials shared with affected application | | High | |
| 7 | Assess regulatory and contractual notification obligations based on data access scope | | High | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Implement a WAF with application-specific tuning and alerting on exploit patterns | WAF | High |
| 2 | Enforce least-privilege for web application service accounts — no OS shell or DB admin access | Access Control | High |
| 3 | Implement secrets management — eliminate hardcoded credentials and insecure config storage | Secrets Management | High |
| 4 | Deploy file integrity monitoring on web root and application directories | Detection | High |
| 5 | Establish a vulnerability and dependency patching cadence with tracked SLAs for critical CVEs | Patch Management | High |
| 6 | Integrate DAST and SAST into the CI/CD pipeline to catch exploitable weaknesses pre-deployment | Secure Development | Medium |
| 7 | Conduct application security testing after significant changes and periodically against production | Testing | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, compromise scope, data impact, and path forward. Suitable for sharing with executive leadership, legal counsel, or regulators alongside the Executive Summary. Address: the vulnerability exploited and affected component, persistence mechanisms identified and removed, credentials and data exposed, downstream system impact, confidence in application integrity post-remediation, and any outstanding notification obligations.]**

tasks.title: Validate and classify web application incident
tasks.description: Determine whether the activity represents a confirmed compromise, attempted exploitation, false positive, vulnerability scan, misconfiguration, denial-of-service condition, or other web application security event. Identify the affected application, service, or component.

tasks.title: Initiate stakeholder and provider coordination
tasks.description: Notify and coordinate with application owners, infrastructure teams, developers, DevOps, cloud teams, security leadership, legal, privacy, and any relevant hosting, CDN, WAF, or managed service providers needed to support response.

tasks.title: Identify affected applications, hosts, and environments
tasks.description: Determine the affected application, hostname, URL paths, APIs, containers, servers, databases, storage, secrets, service accounts, build pipelines, and environments such as production, staging, or development. Document confirmed and suspected scope.

tasks.title: Preserve application, host, and platform evidence
tasks.description: Preserve web server logs, application logs, API gateway logs, WAF logs, CDN logs, container logs, host artifacts, process details, deployment records, access logs, authentication logs, source snapshots, database logs, and relevant cloud telemetry needed for investigation.

tasks.title: Characterize exploitation method and access path
tasks.description: Determine how access was gained, such as SQL injection, remote code execution, authentication bypass, file upload abuse, command injection, deserialization, SSRF, credential compromise, exposed admin interface, plugin or CMS exploitation, or API abuse.

tasks.title: Assess persistence, web shells, and attacker tooling
tasks.description: Identify persistence mechanisms such as web shells, backdoors, malicious scripts, cron jobs, startup items, modified templates, unauthorized admin accounts, malicious plugins, rogue containers, or attacker tooling left on the application or supporting infrastructure.

tasks.title: Determine affected data, credentials, and downstream systems
tasks.description: Assess whether data was accessed, modified, deleted, or exfiltrated, and determine whether secrets, API keys, service credentials, session stores, databases, or downstream systems were impacted. Distinguish suspected impact from confirmed evidence.

tasks.title: Contain affected application paths and infrastructure
tasks.description: Contain the incident by blocking malicious requests, restricting vulnerable endpoints, isolating affected hosts or containers, disabling compromised accounts, removing public exposure where necessary, applying temporary WAF rules, and limiting attacker access while preserving evidence where possible.

tasks.title: Remediate vulnerabilities, malicious artifacts, and access issues
tasks.description: Remove web shells and malicious code, patch exploited vulnerabilities, rotate credentials and secrets, revoke sessions, remove unauthorized users or keys, repair insecure configurations, validate application integrity, and eliminate the original access path.

tasks.title: Assess business, legal, privacy, and regulatory impact
tasks.description: Evaluate the impact to service availability, customer trust, data confidentiality, data integrity, contractual obligations, privacy exposure, legal risk, and regulatory obligations based on the nature of the compromise and affected information.

tasks.title: Validate recovery and increase monitoring
tasks.description: Validate that the application is functioning normally after remediation, confirm malicious access has stopped, increase monitoring on affected application paths and infrastructure, and watch for reinfection, repeat exploitation, or suspicious administrator activity.

tasks.title: Implement security improvements and secure development follow-up
tasks.description: Improve secure coding controls, WAF coverage, logging, alerting, dependency management, secret handling, CI/CD security, access control, patch management, and vulnerability management based on lessons learned from the incident.

tasks.title: Document findings and close case
tasks.description: Document the affected application, exploitation path, malicious artifacts, data impact, containment actions, remediation steps, provider coordination, business impact, and lessons learned. Confirm required follow-up actions are complete before case closure.
